# A compiler warning prints as a GitHub Actions annotation in a GitHub Actions
# run, both when the compiler runs and when the build cache replays its
# output. No output starts with a "# package" line.

env GO111MODULE=off
[!compiler:gc] skip

env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
mkdir $GOCACHE
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=true
env GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$WORK
# An agent marker keeps this from being a CI build, which needs a remote cache.
env CLAUDECODE=1

go build -x lib.go
stderr 'compile( |\.exe"?)'
stderr '^::warning file=gopath/src/lib.go,line=5,col=\d+::performance warning: the pattern of regexp.MustCompile is not constant'
! stderr '^# command-line-arguments'
! stderr '^lib.go:5'

# The second build replays the cached output and annotates it the same way.
go build -x lib.go
! stderr 'compile( |\.exe"?)'
stderr '^::warning file=gopath/src/lib.go,line=5,col=\d+::performance warning'
! stderr '^# command-line-arguments'

# Outside GitHub Actions the replayed warning is a plain line.
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=
go build lib.go
stderr 'lib.go:5:\d+: performance warning'
! stderr '::warning'
! stderr '^# command-line-arguments'

-- lib.go --
package lib

import "regexp"

func Match(pattern, text string) bool { return regexp.MustCompile(pattern).MatchString(text) }
